title: tests.py caps its pytest workers so concurrent sessions do not oversubscribe the host
goal: tests.py runs pytest-xdist with a capped worker count (a KB_TEST_WORKERS setting, and by default a share of the CPUs when other tests.py runs of the clone are live) instead of -n auto, so four sessions' gates on one host do not each start one worker per core and turn tests into timeouts. Answers SP-x2pvljz6: every gate started about 14 workers per session and many fast-test failures were load timeouts that passed alone.
